title: Elon Musk joins 100,000+ signers on a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang — including 5,000+ who say they work at Nvidia
detail:
Elon Musk joins 100,000+ signers on a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang — including 5,000+ who say they work at Nvidia
Rudro Chakrabarti
Sat, November 14, 2026 at 9:25 AM PST 8 min read
NVDA
TSLA
SPCX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Elon Musk wants Jensen Huang back in charge of Nvidia [NASDAQ: NVDA] — and he's putting his name on it.

"A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too," the Tesla and SpaceX CEO [NASDAQ: TSLA] posted on X on Nov. 13.

He isn't alone. As of 10:30 a.m. ET on Nov. 14, an online letter called Stand with Jensen listed more than 100,000 names — including more than 5,000 people who say they currently work at Nvidia.

Huang co-founded the chipmaker in 1993 and led it for 33 years, building it into one of the world's most valuable companies. Nvidia announced Nov. 12 that he had resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. The board accepted his resignation Nov. 11, according to a regulatory filing. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and director Harvey Jones became the board's first-ever chair.

His exit came after reports that he'd had extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspect was recruited by China's top spy agency. Huang has admitted to an affair. Neither he nor Nvidia has been charged with any wrongdoing thus far.

What the Stand with Jensen petition asks for

The Stand with Jensen letter asks the board to "bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, unless and until you can provide compelling evidence that his removal is in NVIDIA's best interests."

Beyond reinstatement, the letter asks the board to disclose the scope, independence and timeline of its investigation, give Huang a chance to respond before any final decision, and publicly explain the evidence behind his removal. The signers say they haven't been shown evidence that the woman at the center of the controversy was a spy, and argue Huang deserves "due process, not mob justice."

The site says it isn't affiliated with Nvidia or Huang. Signers identify themselves, and organizers say they may hold new signatures for review before counting them.

We just published the list of the 10 High P/E Stocks Under the 200-Day SMA, and Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) takes 6th place on our list.

A high price-to-earnings ratio usually reflects substantial expectations for a company's future earnings. But what happens when those expectations remain elevated even as the stock falls below its long-term trading average? That disconnect has become particularly relevant following the recent technology selloff, which has pressured several companies with strong growth prospects but demanding valuations.

The retreat has been especially visible in stocks exposed to artificial intelligence and semiconductor spending. Reuters reported on November 9 that a "month-long swoon" in technology and AI-related stocks in the week ended with the biggest one-day drop for the S&P 500 technology sector in more than six years.

The primary concern for investors is the Democratic victories in the midterm elections, which may lead to sluggish data-center spending, which makes up the center of the market rally. The 200-day simple moving average provides another perspective on these developments. By averaging a stock's closing prices over approximately 200 trading sessions, the indicator helps investors assess its longer-term price trend. A stock trading below this level may be experiencing sustained selling pressure, although the technical signal alone says little about whether its underlying business is undervalued.

title: SpaceX’s S&P 500 Bid Gets New Life as Musk Pitches Tesla Merger
detail:
SpaceX’s S&P 500 Bid Gets New Life as Musk Pitches Tesla Merger
Bloomberg · Photographer: Victor J. Blue/Bloomberg
Jordan Fitzgerald and Lu Wang
Sat, November 14, 2026 at 6:00 AM PST 5 min read
SPCX
TSLA
^GSPC

Trading disclosure

(Bloomberg) -- Just months after SpaceX was denied a swift entry into the S&P 500 Index, Elon Musk may have found a backdoor: Merging with Tesla Inc., one of the stock-market benchmark's biggest members.

Most Read from Bloomberg

'I'm a Piece of Sh--': Jensen Huang's Last Hours as Nvidia CEO

Thousands of US Flights Disrupted as Nationwide Halt Extends

Alice Huang-Linked Firm Procured Banned Nvidia Chips in China

Microsoft Races to Fix Outlook in One of Its Longest Outages

US Flight Chaos Persists With Thousands of Cancellations, Delays

Talks have been progressing toward a tie-up that would consolidate Musk's business empire into a single behemoth spanning from electric cars and AI to satellite launches and social media. A main motivation would almost certainly be unleashing potential synergies as he seeks to push into expensive and speculative ventures like robotic assistants, orbital datacenters and even colonies on Mars.

But possible inclusion in the S&P 500 offers another significant incentive to a man whose nearly $900 billion fortune has relied heavily on salesmanship and a cult-like following among Tesla and SpaceX investors. That's because it would ensure that $16 trillion of passive index-tracking funds hold on to shares of the combined company, regardless of what happens to the outlook or the bottom line.

"If you hold an S&P index fund or ETF in your 401(k) or investment account, the manager of that fund is compelled to buy every stock in the index in proportion to its weight," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers. "As a result, you own all those stocks whether you knowingly intended to or not."

Both Tesla and SpaceX have been burning through billions of dollars in cash, and plan to bleed through more to finance new ventures, even as worries about the sustainability of the AI boom drag on the stock market.

While SpaceX reported its first quarter of positive earnings last month, Tesla has faced inconsistent demand for its cars in the US and mounting competition abroad. It just discontinued the Cybertruck, which became a divisive symbol of Musk's right-wing politics as he became a key adviser to US President Donald Trump after his return to the White House.

The stocks also hover at particularly lofty levels. Even after slipping 13% this year, Tesla is trading at more than 180 times its expected earnings, compared with 18 for the overall S&P 500. Soon after its initial public offering in June, SpaceX commanded a market value of as much as $2.6 trillion, a heady level for a company that had $32 billion in revenue in the 12 months through September.

Elon Musk said it would be an honor to have Huang at Tesla or SpaceX, but made no formal offer or specified a potential role.

President Donald Trump praised Huang and suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook could replace him.

Trump also stated that the FBI was investigating Huang's relationship involving the woman allegedly suspected of being a Chinese spy.

At the start of the week, Nvidia's (NVDA) board publicly expressed "absolute confidence in Jensen and his leadership team." Four days later, CEO Jensen Huang had resigned, effective immediately, leaving the company facing an unexpected leadership transition just days before its next earnings report.

Nvidia said Huang stepped down as president, CEO, and board member. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement. The company is scheduled to report third-quarter results next Tuesday.

The abrupt departure prompted reactions from across the board, including Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk and President Donald Trump. Their comments ranged from Musk suggesting it would be an honor to bring Huang to his companies to Trump publicly floating former Apple CEO Tim Cook as a possible successor.

Nvidia's Board: From 'Confidence In Jensen' To 'Immeasurable Contributions'

"The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team."

– Nvidia Board Statement (November 8, 2026)

Nvidia's board issued the above statement on Sunday while announcing an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. It also said it had "no reason to believe" that national security or Nvidia's confidential information had been compromised.

"Immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."

– Nvidia Board Statement (November 12, 2026)

Four days later, the board's tone had shifted. Its announcement of Huang's departure thanked him for his "immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry," but offered no reason for his resignation and included no statement from Huang.

According to the company's SEC filing, the board accepted Huang's resignation on Nov. 11. Kress will retain her CFO responsibilities while serving as interim CEO. The board said it will consider both internal and external candidates in its search for a permanent chief executive.

This week, NVDA stock logged its longest weekly losing streak since 2012, with its market capitalization sinking by over $1.6 trillion. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Nvidia trended in the 'extremely bullish' territory over the past week, with chatter rising to 'extremely high' from 'high' levels. Platform data showed an uptick of nearly 400% in message volume over the last seven days.

Musk Responds To MKBHD

Brownlee highlighted several restrictions on the Cybercab's newly launched order page in a post on X, including its invite-only availability, limited delivery locations and mandatory monthly subscription.

"Cybercab order page is live. Invite only. Must accept delivery to one of these cities in Texas. Only operates in those existing geofenced areas. Requires a $300 monthly subscription to operate. One vehicle per customer. 'Estimated delivery' December," he wrote.

Marques Brownlee's post on X | @MKBHD/X

Musk responded to the post, saying the vehicle's availability would eventually expand beyond its initial locations.

"It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval," Musk said.

"But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month," Musk added.

The response suggests Tesla could eventually reduce the Cybercab's monthly operating cost from nearly $300 to around $115, although Musk did not provide a timeline for the potential change.

Tesla announced on Friday that "select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use" at an estimated purchase price of $29,990.

title: Tesla Cybercab Now Available For Purchase For Select Customers — But There’s A Catch
detail:
Tesla Cybercab Now Available For Purchase For Select Customers — But There’s A Catch
Stocktwits News Desk
Fri, November 13, 2026 at 10:09 PM PST 4 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Tesla announced that "select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use" at an estimated price of $29,990.

Buyers will also need to pay a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit and subscribe to Tesla's autonomous driving software for $299 per month.

The company estimates that deliveries will begin in December.

Tesla Inc. (TSLA) has begun inviting select customers to purchase its fully autonomous Cybercab, marking a new step in Elon Musk's long-promised robotaxi ambitions.

However, owning the futuristic, two-seater vehicle comes with some significant limitations, including a mandatory monthly software subscription and restrictions on where it can operate.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Tesla shares declined nearly 2% in Friday's regular trading, while falling another 1% in the afterhours session.

Tesla Cybercab Comes With $299 Monthly Subscription

In posts on X on Friday, Tesla announced that "select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use" at an estimated price of $29,990.

Buyers will also need to pay a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit and subscribe to Tesla's autonomous driving software for $299 per month.

The company estimates that deliveries will begin in December.

The two-door vehicle, which has no steering wheel or pedals, was previously deployed exclusively in Tesla's robotaxi fleet.

However, personal ownership does not mean buyers can immediately use the vehicles anywhere they want. Tesla clarified in the fine print that personally owned Cybercabs will only operate "in supported service areas."

Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's head of AI, added that the vehicles will "work unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as" the company's existing Robotaxi service.

There is also a catch for prospective buyers hoping to turn their vehicles into money-making robotaxis. Tesla's current personal-use offering does not allow owners to immediately operate them as commercial fleet vehicles.

Regulatory Hurdles And Robotaxi Ambitions

The announcement comes after years of promises from Musk about bringing fully autonomous vehicles to consumers.

In 2016, Tesla claimed that all vehicles it was producing had the hardware necessary to become fully self-driving. Three years later, Musk predicted the company would have "over a million robotaxis" on the roads by 2020.

Those ambitions have yet to fully materialize, although Tesla has made progress with its Robotaxi service, which began operating Model Y SUVs in Austin, Texas, in June 2025 before expanding to other cities in Texas and Florida.

Tesla Inc. (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk, Fundstrat's Tom Lee, Shopify CEO Tobi Lutke and others have joined to sign a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia Corp. (NVDA).

Nvidia shares fell more than 2% in Friday's regular trading, declining over 1% more during the afterhours session.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

What The 'Stand With Jensen' Petition Is About

The petition, "Stand with Jensen," had about 36,000 signatures at the time of writing. The tracker lists nearly 2,700 existing Nvidia employees among those who have signed it, while over 20,000 existing Nvidia shareholders are said to have been among those who have pledged support for Huang to be reinstated as the company's chief.

"A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too," said Musk in a post on X.

The signatories said that Huang should be reinstated while an independent investigation into the allegations surrounding him establishes the facts.

In the open letter, the group praised Huang for spending 33 years building Nvidia, arguing that his leadership and contributions to the company deserve fairness and due process rather than an abrupt removal.

They also expressed concern that Huang was removed without meaningful due process, noting that they had not been presented with evidence substantiating allegations that the woman at the center of the controversy was a spy.

They urged the board to ensure an independent investigation, give Huang a fair opportunity to respond, disclose the inquiry's scope and timeline, and publicly explain the evidence and reasoning behind its decisions.

The letter emphasized that Huang should remain accountable, but argued that accountability must be based on evidence and a fair hearing.

Why Huang Stepped Down

Huang announced his decision to step down as Nvidia CEO, President, and a member of the board effective immediately on Thursday.
